history.sg_progress: The vendor registration and outreach team has initiated discussions with the engineering category teams to develop a strategy to increase the number of potential vendors and seek ways to reach out to those vendors who meet the Organization’s requirements in accordance with the demand plan. This will include market research and outreach through Member States, with the goal of identifying new solutions for the design and production of prefabricated accommodation structures. The Administration will also identify upcoming international exhibitions or trade fairs that provide opportunities to learn about engineering innovations and to connect with potential suppliers and industry experts worldwide in order to expand the Organization’s network of suppliers, in particular in the areas of prefabricated construction, sustainable building technologies and innovative housing solutions.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration develop a strategy to increase the number of potential vendors in the engineering, design and construction category that are interested in working with the United Nations.
history.administration_response: The recommendation is under implementation. The Enabling and Outreach Service of the Office of Supply Chain Management continues to collaborate with relevant category management teams to offer support in organizing outreach activities to increase the number of potential vendors for the various core categories. The Administration wishes to highlight that engineering, design and construction is considered a bespoke category; the Office of Supply Chain Management provides support for this category as and when needed. In that regard, the strategy to enable the Office to increase the number of potential vendors for this category is to: (a) identify upcoming solicitation requirements by reviewing the rolling supply chain plan; (b) collaborate with client entities and other stakeholders on major solicitation processes entailing design and construction services in order to obtain better feedback from clients on the specificity of their requirements, so that the outreach strategy can provide effective results; (c) analyse the specific market conditions, including by identifying qualified vendors already registered with the United Nations Global Marketplace and (d) reach out to other qualified vendors that can contribute to achieving the end results of effective international competition, including through advertisements, category-specific business seminars and/or outreach to Member States in order to inform them of upcoming solicitation requirements and request them to share such information with their business communities, so as to broaden outreach to the relevant vendor base. In view of these considerations, the target date for the development and implementation of the strategy will be the fourth quarter of 2025, with relevant solicitation processes expected to be conducted by then.
history.board_assessment: The initial target date is June 2025 and work is ongoing. The Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The engineering, design and construction category is now considered a bespoke category. There is therefore no specific category lead or category team in place to liaise with. Furthermore, the scope of the quarterly review of the supply chain demand plan does not include the engineering, design and construction category, as it is focused on core categories only. Due to the current financial situation, there have been limited opportunities to identify suitable solicitations, as many construction projects have been deferred or put on hold. The Enabling and Outreach Service has recently identified a potential project that would allow it to increase the outreach effort in order to identify additional vendors.
